value.overview: The Mountain Elaenia (Elaenia frantzii) is a small, active tyrant flycatcher of the highlands of Central America and northern South America. It is associated especially with humid montane forest, cloud forest edges, secondary growth, and other partially open habitats. The species is generally plain-looking but has a subtle pale eye ring, two light wing bars, and a short crest. In Costa Rica it is a familiar resident or seasonal elevational migrant of the country's mountain ranges.
value.classification: The Mountain Elaenia belongs to the tyrant flycatcher family, Tyrannidae, and the elaenia genus Elaenia. It is a passerine bird.
value.identification: This small flycatcher has olive-green to grayish upperparts, a gray head, a pale throat, and whitish to pale yellow underparts. Its bill is short and broad, with a dark upper mandible and a paler lower mandible. Two pale wing bars, pale feather edges, and a light eye ring are useful field marks. The crown may show a small crest when the bird is alert. It can resemble other elaenias, so voice, habitat, and elevation are helpful for confirmation.
value.rangeHabitat: The Mountain Elaenia has a disjunct range from southern Mexico through Central America and from Colombia and Venezuela into the northern Andes. In Costa Rica, the nominate form occurs mainly in the highlands and mountain ranges, including suitable habitats in the Central and southern parts of the country. It uses humid montane forest, cloud-forest margins, secondary woodland, forest clearings, shrubby edges, and sometimes lightly modified areas. It is usually found from roughly 1,200 to 2,500 meters, with lower seasonal movements.
value.migrationStatus: In Costa Rica, the Mountain Elaenia is not a long-distance migrant but appears to make regular elevational movements. It breeds at higher elevations and may descend to lower mountain zones after breeding, especially from late summer through the nonbreeding season. The timing and extent of these movements vary and are not fully understood. Elsewhere in northern Central America it is considered largely resident.
value.breeding: Most available breeding information comes from Costa Rica. Breeding generally occurs in the higher parts of the species' elevational range, with the season extending at least from early April through June. The species builds a small open cup nest, usually placed in vegetation above the ground, although exact nest-site details can vary. Pairs defend breeding territories and adults care for the young. Outside the breeding season, individuals may move downslope and appear less closely tied to particular territories.
value.dietFeeding: The Mountain Elaenia eats insects, other small arthropods, and small fruits. Fruit may form a larger part of its diet than in many related elaenias. It usually forages alone in dense foliage at several levels of the forest, taking food by gleaning from leaves and twigs, briefly hovering, or making short sallies to capture insects. It may visit fruiting trees with other Mountain Elaenias and occasionally joins mixed-species feeding flocks.
value.behavior: This species is an alert, active, and vocal forest-edge flycatcher. It often perches quietly within foliage before making short flights to collect insects or moving to another branch. Individuals may flick or raise the crest when attentive. Mountain Elaenias are commonly seen singly or in pairs, although several may gather at fruiting trees. Their behavior and presence in Costa Rica can change seasonally as birds move between higher breeding areas and lower elevations.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population is not considered to be undergoing a major decline, although precise population data are limited.
